memo.verdict: PARK. Do not progress MMB-FR (Lagardere) to Early-Stage Assessment. Medium conviction. Direction stated explicitly in the memo: bearish on Lagardere SA as an investable Viewforth position, neutral to constructive on Lagardere as an operating company. The memo's central finding is that these two verdicts genuinely diverge. The memo quotes the Risks report's own Stage Progression recommendation, "we recommend a strict hold-and-watch stance until net leverage drops below 1.5x and antitrust risks resolve", and ADOPTS it in full. Park is the Viewforth Triaging equivalent of hold-and-watch. There is no conflict to defend: the memo reached the same verdict from Element work the Risks report does not itself assess. Named conditions for progression: net leverage below 1.5x on rolling recurring EBITDA, sustained across two reporting periods rather than at a single year-end and without reliance on one-off asset inflows; resolution of the European Commission gun-jumping proceedings against Vivendi; minority dividend outflows falling below EUR 30m annualised from the FY25 level of EUR 53m total; any event that materially widens the public free float from its sub-10% level, including a placing, a Louis Hachette Group restructuring, or a change in Qatar Holding's 11.47% stake.
case: The memo's argument runs in this order.

First, the change forces are real, quantified and tied for best in the peer set. Element E1 Required Attribute RA1 grades [B], the highest Required-Attribute grade in the memo alongside E11.RA1. External tailwinds: global air passenger volumes reached 9.8 billion in 2025, up 3.7%, with a doubling projected by 2043 at a 3.8% compound rate; Amsterdam Schiphol duty free was consolidated from May 2025 on a 70% stake, adding roughly EUR 100m of annual revenue and a EUR 184m positive scope effect in FY25; Auckland, Geneva, Verona, London Luton and Heathrow Terminal 2 Relay awards extend multi-year visibility on concession terms averaging eight years; French middle-school curriculum reform is worth roughly plus 1.5% like-for-like from late 2026, with French publishing up 1% in Q1 2026 against a market down 6%; the USD 1.5bn Anthropic settlement pool could yield EUR 0.40 to EUR 0.70 per share after tax. Internal self-help: mainland China network streamlining completed in H1 2026, removing a EUR 55m annual recurring EBIT drag; leverage fell from 3.00x in 2023 to 2.40x in 2024 to 1.96x at FY25, beating the sub-2.0x target a year early; Paris Match sold to LVMH for EUR 120m enterprise value and Prisma luxury titles to Vivendi for EUR 10.4m; Frederic Chevalier succeeded Dag Rasmussen as Travel Retail chief executive on 1 March 2026 with Jerome Petit as deputy from June 2026; board games grew 9% like-for-like in H1 2026 on the Flip 7 release.

Second, the base those forces act on is not robust. Element E1 Required Attribute RA2 grades [C]. Headwind density is the weakest input in the case and grades [D] on its own Core Question: Middle East revenue down 28% like-for-like in H1 2026 across Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Saudi hubs, though the region is only 1% of H1 2026 group revenue; EUR 113m of FY25 and EUR 100m of H1 2026 currency translation drag; jet fuel up 21% to 25% in mid-2026 with US June airfares up 26.5% year on year; concession lease expense historically reaching 30% of sales for leading duty-free operators; French written-press advertising down 9.4% in 2025. The delivery record is genuinely good, an honest-tracker archetype beating guidance in FY22, FY23, FY24 and FY25, but the FY25 deleveraging print relied on EUR 85m of non-recurring inflows.
counter_case: The memo carried a counter-view on every in-scope Element and states the strongest opposing case in full force.

The central counter is that a third-percentile multiple on record earnings is itself the change force. Asia break-even plus the copyright windfall could force a re-rating without any ownership event. The memo rejects this because the 15% discount is applied at enterprise-value level and is therefore structural rather than sentiment, but it records the counter as the strongest single argument against the verdict.
triggers: Progression conditions. Net leverage below 1.5x on rolling recurring EBITDA, sustained across two reporting periods and without one-off asset inflows. Resolution of the European Commission gun-jumping proceedings against Vivendi. Minority dividend outflows below EUR 30m annualised against the FY25 level of EUR 53m total. Any event materially widening the public free float from its sub-10% level.

Confirming triggers for the bear reading. A second consecutive period of rising net debt without a seasonal explanation, or minority dividend outflows above EUR 60m. The memo names the free float as what would change the verdict fastest, since every other objection is a matter of degree while the float constraint is binary and structural.

Key questions for any future Early-Stage Assessment. Whether US airport concession margins can expand while minority leakage falls, which the memo identifies as the Risks report's own stated thesis-overturning condition. Whether the EUR 0.40 to EUR 0.70 per share copyright settlement converts to cash within eighteen months and whether it is applied to debt reduction rather than distribution. Whether the H1 2026 leverage reading of 2.2x is seasonal working-capital drag or genuine slippage, given net debt rose EUR 195m from the December 2025 close while falling EUR 201m year on year.

Element-level monitorables. Q3 2026 Asia-Pacific segment profitability for losses compressed below EUR 15m annualised, by 31-Oct-26. Middle East like-for-like revenue stabilisation by Q4 2026, per the earnings review's own change-my-mind trigger. Concession rent as a percentage of Travel Retail sales at each interim result from H1 2027. Further landlord in-housing precedents after GMR Delhi and Hyderabad. Re-score of Element E5 when the outstanding Thematic 4 batch re-score completes. Re-test of the false-friend guardrail if minority dividend outflows fall below EUR 30m annualised. Re-test of Element E7 only if the driver count falls to three or fewer.
Expected timeline. Quarterly park review, with an interim check at the Q3 2026 results in October 2026, when Asia-Pacific segment profitability and Middle East stabilisation both report.

Data gaps and conflicts the memo flagged, all carried forward. The dashboard valuation feed is flagged stale: its stored 7.60x against stored 24-month-forward earnings per share of EUR 2.3332 implies a strike price near EUR 17.73, not the live EUR 19.14, so the memo carries the arithmetic-consistent 8.20x and treats the percentile of 3 as directionally reliable rather than precise. The covenant threshold is stated as 3.00x in the change-forces digest and Risks report and as 3.25x recurring EBITDA in the leadership-foundations and earnings-review reports; both are carried and neither preferred. H1 2026 cash flow from operations appears as EUR 70m in the Risks report and EUR 84m in the leadership-foundations report; no grade relies on either. FY25 Travel Retail margin appears as 5.5% and 5.45%; the memo uses 5.45%. FY23 group revenue appears as both EUR 8,081m and EUR 8,111m and neither was used. Minority outflows reconcile as EUR 53m group total, EUR 45m US subset and EUR 28m half-year. The context pack's coverage.md wrongly states "Above-floor reports present: none" when four above-floor families are present and were read; flagged for the context-assembly owner. Four of six peers (Axfood, Jumbo, HAL Trust, Redcare) have neither a master digest nor ratings on disk, so the effective comparison set is three names, which the memo states as a limitation on grade precision. The Wisdom Library model list is empty for this ticker. No self-initiated research queries were run, per the Triaging rule.
